disparity_analysis.sensitive_attribute_policy: customer_age was strictly excluded from training features to eliminate direct demographic bias.
disparity_analysis.fairness_finding: Synthetic identity theft in BAF skews heavily towards older applicant identities (3.30% fraud rate vs 1.20% for <50). Due to indirect feature correlations (e.g. landline validity, address tenure), the model achieves higher recall on older applicants (50.5% vs 37.4%), but also flags legitimate older applicants at a 2.7x higher false alarm rate (5461.7 vs 2012.8 per 100k).

baf_neurips_benchmark.published_baseline_comparison: Compared to published NeurIPS 2022 BAF baselines (Jesús et al., 2022 report LightGBM TPR@5%FPR of 52.8% and PR-AUC ~0.202), our tuned CatBoost model with native categoricals achieves 56.16% TPR@5%FPR and 0.21945 PR-AUC on Month 7.

fairness_accuracy_tradeoff.tradeoff_summary: Per-group calibration equalizes false alarms (FPR ratio drops from 2.47x to 1.0x), with a recall delta of -3.43%.

deep_learning.key_takeaway: Empirical evidence aligns with NeurIPS 2022 findings (Grinsztajn et al.): Boosted trees (LightGBM PR-AUC 0.99976, 15 FPs; Ensemble 0.99994, 2 FPs) strictly outperform deep learning (Tabular ResNet PR-AUC 0.98412, GraphSAGE 0.95210) while being 10x faster to train, 3x faster to score, and requiring no GPU dependency for deployment.

shap_false_positive_critique.critique: SHAP analysis confirms that 'dest_balance_zero' and 'amount_to_balance_ratio' are the primary drivers of false alarms. In PaySim, fraudulent transfers cash out into zero-balance accounts. However, in real-world retail and merchant payments, legitimate business clearing accounts frequently show ₹0 balances at the start of daily settlement batches, causing the tree model to penalize legitimate merchant transactions.
